method: Nelson model with uniform operational profile (as specified by De Angelis point 4.c)
rationale: Under a uniform operational profile, every test case is assumed equally likely to be triggered. R is the proportion of test executions that succeed.

C_B_original_class.interpretation: Perfect empirical reliability over the executed test suite.

C_B_variants.interpretation: All Copilot refactorings preserved full reliability under the test suite.

C_A_classes.reason: C_A_1 and C_A_2 do not compile (5 and 100 errors respectively). C_A_0's complex methods (Select/ExpContext/MetaDataRepository dependencies) cannot be tested in isolation without instantiating the full OpenJPA runtime, which is incompatible with modern Java. Documented as a threat to validity.

caveats_and_threats: Mutation analysis revealed 75% of Math.java code (NO_COVERAGE) is never executed by our test suite. R=1.0 reflects reliability over the covered ~25-60% portion only.
86 tests is a small sample; results have wide confidence intervals.
Uniform operational profile is an idealization; real production usage would weight some methods (e.g., getType, calculateValue) more heavily.
We did NOT need to disable any failing tests in this experiment (point 4.c bullet).
